newsitem.title: BRAZIL: BankBoston's Ayers sees further Fed tightening.
newsitem.headline: BankBoston's Ayers sees further Fed tightening.

text.p: BankBoston Corp chief economist Wayne Ayers said the Federal Reserve Board would likely raise short-term U.S. interest rates another 25 basis points this year, but he sees the U.S. long bond rate falling significantly by the end of the year.
"The consensus now is that the Fed will hold, but I think they will tighten," Ayers told foreign correspondents at a briefing at the bank's Brazilian headquarters in Sao Paulo.
Ayers, on a week-long trip to South America, said another hike of 25 basis points would be consistent with the Fed's goal of 2.5-3.0 percent real economic growth this year.

Such a hike, however, would cause only a "short-lived" reaction in the U.S. Treasury market, he added. Ayers forecast the yield on the 30-year U.S. Treasury bond would fall to 6.25-6.50 percent by the end of the year from a current rate of 6.80 percent.
"While the (U.S.) economy is on track, the pace of the economy will slow," Ayers said.

If the Fed raises rates by 25 bp, on top of March's 25 bp hike, there will be no need for further tightening, he said. The Treasury market could then settle in for a steady rally through the end of the year, he added.
The Federal Reserve's policy-making Federal Open Market Committee will consider policy moves at its next meeting early next month.
Ayers, who has been BankBoston's chief economist for eight years, is a former economist for the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System in Washington, D.C.
